messages.content: I need to start planning a Savannah wedding weekend for my spouse and me. We can leave Denver Friday, June 20, and come back Monday, June 23. The ceremony is Saturday at 4:00 near Forsyth Park, and there is a family brunch Sunday at 11:00 by the riverfront.
I’ll compare flights for two adults and one room for three nights. Before I narrow it down, how late can you arrive Friday, and do you want to stay closer to the ceremony or the Sunday brunch?
I would rather be checked in by dinner Friday. I’m not sure about the hotel area yet. That is part of what I need help deciding.

The strongest Friday flight is a one-stop itinerary through Atlanta, leaving Denver at 8:20 a.m. and arriving Savannah at 2:18 p.m. It is $487 per person round trip with regular economy fares. A less expensive connection through Dallas leaves at 10:05 a.m. and arrives at 5:42 p.m. for $421 per person, but a modest delay could push check-in well past dinner. There is also a 6:10 a.m. departure through Houston arriving at 1:06 p.m. for $458 per person. Would you trade the early start for the extra arrival cushion?
Not at 6:10. The 8:20 flight sounds like the workable one. What are the Monday choices? I do not want to leave at dawn after a family weekend.

The $487 itinerary pairs with a 1:35 p.m. Monday departure from Savannah, connecting in Atlanta and reaching Denver at 5:58 p.m. A 4:20 p.m. departure reaches Denver at 9:46 p.m. and raises the fare to $536 per person. There is also an 11:15 a.m. option arriving at 3:52 p.m. for $469 per person.
Keep the 1:35 return in the comparison. That gives us breakfast and enough time to get to the airport without using the whole day.

That round trip totals $974 for two before checked bags or seat fees. Both directions have one connection in Atlanta, and the layovers are 58 minutes outbound and 1 hour 12 minutes returning. The Friday arrival leaves roughly 90 minutes for baggage claim, the airport drive, and hotel check-in before 4:00 p.m.
Good. Now compare a few hotels. One near Forsyth Park and one or two closer to the river, with all mandatory charges included.

Near the ceremony, the Forsyth Park Inn has a queen room at $238 nightly and a three-night total of $806.41 with tax; breakfast and parking are separate, but there is no mandatory resort or destination fee. It is about a 7-minute walk to the ceremony area, 8 to 12 minutes by car to the riverfront brunch, and about 25 minutes from the airport in ordinary traffic. A king room raises the total to $869.76.
A queen is not ideal for both of us. What do the riverfront places look like?

The River Street Hotel has a king at $259 nightly, plus a mandatory $32 nightly destination charge. Its three-night total is $1,018.93 including that charge and taxes. It is a 4-minute walk to the brunch, about 12 minutes by car to the ceremony, and usually 20 to 25 minutes from the airport. The Bay Street House is two blocks inland, with a king at $247 nightly and no mandatory property fee; total is $864.58. It is an 8-minute walk to brunch, 9 to 12 minutes by car to the ceremony, and roughly 22 minutes from the airport.
So the Bay Street one is almost the same total as the king near Forsyth. Is there a practical difference beyond which event is walkable?

Yes. Around Forsyth Park, Saturday is simpler and the setting is quieter at night, but you would likely use a car twice on Sunday for brunch. Bay Street gives you more restaurants within a short walk Friday and Sunday, while Saturday requires a rideshare to the ceremony. Riverfront streets can be congested, but Bay Street avoids the steepest cobblestone access and is easier for pickup than a hotel directly on River Street.
How much time should we allow for the Saturday ride from Bay Street? We need to be seated before 4:00, not arriving at the door then.

I would request the car at 3:10 p.m. The drive is commonly 10 to 15 minutes, but wedding traffic and pickup delays could make it 25. That should put you near Forsyth Park around 3:30, leaving time to walk to the venue and be seated. From the Forsyth hotel, you could leave on foot around 3:25.
And on Monday, is the airport meaningfully easier from either area for the 1:35 flight?

Not enough to drive the hotel decision. From Bay Street, leaving around 10:50 a.m. should get you to SAV near 11:20. From the Forsyth area, 10:45 is safer because the route can take a few minutes longer. Both provide about two hours before departure, assuming you check out on time.
Does either hotel include parking? We may rent a car if family plans spread out.

Neither includes it. Forsyth Park Inn offers valet at $38 per night, while Bay Street House charges $46 per night. Adding three nights of parking and tax would put the approximate lodging totals at $997 near Forsyth and $1,019 on Bay Street. A rental car would also sit unused for the two scheduled events, so rideshares are likely less expensive unless additional family visits require several trips.
Then no rental car for now. Can you put together the best combination and one backup? Do not book anything yet.

Best balance: the 8:20 a.m. Friday flight through Atlanta, arriving SAV at 2:18 p.m.; Bay Street House king room for three nights at $864.58; and the 1:35 p.m. Monday return through Atlanta, arriving Denver at 5:58 p.m. Air and lodging total $1,838.58 for two before bags, seats, meals, and local transportation. Friday airport-to-hotel travel should be about 25 minutes, Saturday’s ceremony is a short rideshare away, and Sunday brunch is an 8-minute walk.
What is the backup, and what would make you switch to it?

The backup uses the same flights with the Forsyth Park Inn king room at $869.76, for a combined $1,843.76. I would switch if the Saturday venue confirms difficult vehicle access, if more family activities are added around Forsyth Park, or if a quieter location matters more than walking to brunch and restaurants. The lodging price difference is only $5.18, so location and room conditions should decide it.
Can you check cancellation terms and whether either room requires prepayment? That may settle it.

Bay Street House allows cancellation without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time on June 18 and takes a one-night deposit at booking. The remaining balance is due at checkout. Forsyth Park Inn’s quoted rate is fully refundable through 3:00 p.m. on June 19 and requires only a card guarantee, with payment due at the property. The flight fares can be held only until midnight today at the quoted prices and are nonrefundable but changeable for a fare difference.

The Forsyth terms are better, but I think the Bay Street location fits the whole weekend better. Leave that as the leading plan and note the Forsyth king as the backup. I’ll confirm with my spouse before we reserve.

The leading plan is Bay Street House, June 20-23, one king room for two adults at $864.58 including taxes and all mandatory charges. The backup is the Forsyth Park Inn king at $869.76. Flights remain the 8:20 a.m. Denver departure Friday, arriving Savannah at 2:18 p.m. through Atlanta, and the 1:35 p.m. Monday departure, arriving Denver at 5:58 p.m., also through Atlanta, for $974 total. Nothing has been booked. The flight quote expires at midnight, while hotel availability and rates can change before you confirm.
